tax.text: She supported the One Big Beautiful Bill, which she said would cut taxes for working families and small businesses.
tax.quote: The One Big Beautiful Bill delivers on the mandate the American people voted for by: cutting taxes for our working families and small businesses

wages.text: She opposed a proposed federal $15 minimum wage, arguing it could cost jobs and harm small businesses.
wages.quote: a federal, nationwide mandate to raise the minimum wage to $15 per hour, will put us right back to where we were months ago.

trade.text: She introduced a bill to strengthen trade remedy laws and address trade practices she said disadvantage American manufacturers.
trade.quote: Our legislation will allow American workers to compete on a more level playing field by cracking down on exploitative trade practices from countries like China

debt.text: She introduced resolutions to preserve Social Security and Medicare while addressing federal debt negotiations.
debt.quote: House Republicans are united in our solemn commitment to protect and preserve Social Security and Medicare

housing.text: She introduced the Housing Supply Expansion Act to increase the supply of affordable housing.
housing.quote: The Housing Supply Expansion Act will help increase the supply of affordable housing by removing archaic red-tape requirements under the Davis-Bacon Act.

safety.text: She requested federal funding for Dallas police technology and marine-patrol equipment to improve crime response and enforcement.
safety.quote: This project expands the Dallas Police Department’s Drone as a First Responder (DFR) program by deploying additional drone systems integrated with the Department’s Fusion Center and real-time crime analysis operations.

immigration.text: She introduced a bill intended to pressure sanctuary jurisdictions to cooperate with federal immigration enforcement and deportations.
immigration.quote: I’m introducing this bill to support President Trump’s plan to deport criminal illegal aliens by leveraging the power of the purse to pressure local governments to cooperate with federal immigration enforcement.

guns.text: She opposed federal background-check bills, saying they would infringe on Second Amendment rights.
guns.quote: Rep. Beth Van Duyne (TX-24) today spoke on the floor of the House of Representatives in opposition to H.R. 8 and H.R. 1446, legislation that would infringe on American's Second Amendment rights.

abortion.text: She spoke in opposition to a bill she called the Abortion on Demand Act and advocated support for expectant mothers instead.
abortion.quote: Instead of promoting ways for women to end their pregnancies, we should be helping expectant mothers find the medical, emotional, and financial support they need.

gender.toward: rules based on sex at birth
gender.text: She voted for the Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act, which based athletic Title IX rules on reproductive biology and genetics at birth.
gender.quote: Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act

cannabis.text: In a candidate questionnaire, she disagreed with legalizing recreational marijuana.
cannabis.quote:
I support the legalization of recreational marijuana.

Disagree

health.text: She has advocated expanding private insurance options and marketplace competition rather than a one-size-fits-all approach.
health.quote: Congress needs to be focused on expanding health insurance options to lower costs, have more personalized coverage and put patients in direct relationships with physicians.

energy.text: She supported legislation to increase domestic energy production and said energy production at home can help lower costs.
energy.quote: As a Texan, Congresswoman Van Duyne understands that an energy-dominant America is essential for lowering costs, fighting inflation, driving a resurgence in manufacturing, and stabilizing global markets.

voting.text: She reintroduced a bill requiring states to verify potential voters' immigration status when requested by state officials.
voting.quote: This bill will require U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) to verify and provide the immigration status of potential voters, when requested to do so by a state Attorney General or Secretary of State

tax.text: He calls for lower taxes for working families while also proposing expanded assistance programs and Medicaid incentives.
tax.quote: Lower taxes for working families earning less than $400,000 per year.

trade.text: He says he would end tariffs that raise costs for Texas families and businesses.
trade.quote: End wasteful tariffs that raise costs on Texas families and businesses

schools.text: He supports fully funding public schools and opposes education vouchers.
schools.quote: Fight to reform our federal school funding formula to step in where the state cheaped out and fully fund all public schools.

immigration.text: He supports expanding and streamlining legal immigration pathways while also proposing border-security measures.
immigration.quote: Expand and streamline legal pathways for workers and families

abortion.text: His campaign lists restoring abortion rights among his priorities.
abortion.quote: Kevin’s top priorities include affordable housing, restoring checks & balances, medicare for all, immigration reform, protecting civil liberties, tuition-free public college & trade education, restoring abortion rights, and building an economy that works for everyone — not billionaires.

health.text: He supports universal health coverage and expanded public programs while retaining the option to buy private insurance.
health.quote: Prioritize working with Congress to finally fix our broken healthcare system and pass Universal Health Coverage. I do not support banning private health insurance.
